comments.content: `POLICY_MANAGER` is a `static final` field assigned in a static initializer. If `isEnabledForTest()` is false, it's set to `null`, but the field is not declared `@Nullable`. More importantly, `newNodeGrant` and `revokeNodeGrants` dereference `POLICY_MANAGER` without a null check in `revokeNodeGrants` (line ~130). `newNodeGrant` guards with `if (POLICY_MANAGER == null)`, but `revokeNodeGrants` does not, so calling it when entitlements are disabled will NPE. `ESIntegTestCase` calls `TEST_ENTITLEMENTS.revokeNodeGrants()` unconditionally, which will throw when `es.entitlement.enableForTests` is false (the default).

`revokeNodeGrants()` dereferences `POLICY_MANAGER` without a null check. When entitlements are disabled for tests (the default), `POLICY_MANAGER` is null and this will NPE. Add a null guard like in `newNodeGrant`.

`initialize(Path tempDir)` puts `List.of(tempDir)` into `BASE_DIR_PATHS` for TEMP. If `tempDir` is null (which the old `TestEntitlementBootstrap.bootstrap` explicitly allowed via `zeroOrOne`), `List.of(null)` throws NPE. `BootstrapForTesting` passes `javaTmpDir` which may be null in some environments. Consider handling null like the previous implementation did.

The `NodeGrant.close()` method is a no-op (the `onClose.accept(this)` call is commented out). This means `MockNode.awaitClose` calling `IOUtils.closeWhileHandlingException(entitlementGrant)` does nothing, and grants are only cleaned up via `revokeNodeGrants()` at the cluster level. This is intentional per the comment, but it means `newNodeGrant` returns a `Closeable` that silently does nothing, which is misleading. Consider documenting this more clearly or returning a no-op marker type.

`newNodeGrant` unwraps `FilterPath` from `configPath` but does not unwrap it from the paths derived from settings (homeDir, dataDirs, etc.). The old `TestEntitlementBootstrap` used `absolutePath` with `@SuppressForbidden` to resolve via the default filesystem, which is preserved in `NodeGrant.absolutePath`. However, `configPath` is passed in already-unwrapped here, while `NodeGrant.configDir()` returns it directly. This looks consistent, but verify that `configPath` passed from `InternalTestCluster` (via `nodeConfigurationSource.nodeConfigPath(nodeId)`) is not a `FilterPath` that needs unwrapping in other code paths.

`setEntitledTestPackages` now resets to `TEST_FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE_PREFIXES` when called with no args, and always concatenates with `TEST_FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE_PREFIXES` rather than `this.entitledTestPackages`. This is a behavior change: previously, calling `setEntitledTestPackages` twice would accumulate. Now the second call discards the first call's packages. Verify this is intended — the `TestEntitlementsRule` calls `setEntitledTestPackages()` (no args) in the finally block to reset, which relies on this new behavior. But if any test calls it multiple times expecting accumulation, this will break.

`awaitClose` now closes `entitlementGrant` instead of unregistering node base dirs. Since `NodeGrant.close()` is a no-op (see TestEntitlementsRule), this effectively does nothing. The comment about `wipePendingDataDirectories` and ES-10920 was removed, but the underlying issue (grants not being revoked on node close) remains. This is fine if intentional, but the removal of the explanatory comment makes the no-op less obvious to future readers.

`TEST_ENTITLEMENTS.revokeNodeGrants()` is called unconditionally after closing the test cluster. As noted, `revokeNodeGrants` will NPE when entitlements are disabled (the default). This will break all integration tests that don't enable entitlements.

`TEST_ENTITLEMENTS` is declared as a `@ClassRule` on `ESTestCase`. JUnit `@ClassRule` fields must be `public static` and implement `TestRule` — this is satisfied. However, `TestEntitlementsRule.apply` asserts `description.isSuite()`. When a `@ClassRule` is inherited by subclasses, JUnit may invoke `apply` with a non-suite description in some edge cases (e.g., when the rule is applied to a `Suite` that wraps a single test). Verify this assertion holds across all test runners used in the codebase (e.g., parameterized tests, `LuceneTestCase` subclasses).

The `@ClassRule` is `static final` and shared across all subclasses. `TestEntitlementsRule.apply` uses a static `AtomicBoolean active` to detect parallel suite execution and throws `AssertionError` if two suites run concurrently. This is a hard failure mode — if any test infrastructure runs suites in parallel (e.g., Gradle parallel test execution within a single JVM), all tests will fail. The old `@BeforeClass`/`@AfterClass` approach didn't have this restriction. Confirm that parallel suite execution within a single JVM is not supported/expected.

`TEST_ENTITLEMENTS.newNodeGrant(settings, null)` is called with `configPath = null`. In `newNodeGrant`, `configPath` is unwrapped in a while loop — `null instanceof FilterPath` is false, so it's fine. But `NodeGrant.configDir()` handles null by falling back to `homeDir().resolve("config")`. This matches the old behavior. OK.

In the node restart path, `nodeGrantProvider.create(finalSettings, null)` is called with `configPath = null`, whereas the initial node creation at line ~795 passes the actual `configPath`. This means on restart, the config dir grant will be computed from `homeDir().resolve("config")` instead of the actual config path. If the node was originally created with a custom config path, the restart will register a different (wrong) config dir. This is a behavior regression compared to the old code which used `getEnvironment().configDir()` on unregister.
